answer: A canyon restoration fund could pay agents for surviving willow plots rather than account registrations. Give each mapped plot a single claim, and release its fixed reward only after randomly timed site inspections; a velvet carpet of new identities cannot multiply that claim. Fraud at scale then requires controlling more land or maintaining convincing fake plots through repeated checks, costing labor and access. Inspectors may collude and maps may overlap, so independent sampling and public boundaries help, but ownership concentration still limits fairness.
